---
applyTo: "**/*.md"
description: "Voice and structure rules for every markdown piece in this kit"
---
# Writing voice

## Spelling and punctuation
- Australian English: organise, colour, programme, licence (noun), centre, analyse.
- No em dashes or en dashes in prose. Use " - " (spaced hyphen), a comma, a colon or a full stop. Straight quotes; no unicode arrows inside sentences.

## Word watchlist: replace with the specific word, delete the sentence, or keep on purpose. Three in one paragraph is a fail.
delve, leverage, unlock, seamless, game-changing, utilise, enhance, harness, streamline, navigate (non-physical), showcase, underscore, foster, robust, comprehensive, crucial, pivotal, landscape, journey, "it's worth noting".
Also cut: "at its core", "in conclusion", "ultimately", "moreover", "a testament to", "a diverse range of", "in a world where".

## Sentences
- Mix lengths. In any five sentences: one under 8 words, one over 25. Establish a pattern, then break it once per paragraph.
- Vary openers. Three sentences in a row starting with "The" or "We" is a rewrite.
- At most one "not X, it's Y" per page. No reflex triads. No rhetorical question answered in the next line.
- Verbs over nominalisations: "we built" not "the implementation of".
- End important sentences on a stressed word, not on "-ation", "-ity" or "-ing".
- Contractions in posts, emails and talk tracks. Formal documents (two-pagers, playbooks) may skip them.

## Paragraphs
- 1 to 4 sentences. One paragraph per page may run longer when the argument needs it.
- Read the first sentence of each paragraph in order: together they must carry the argument.
- No bridge sentences whose only job is to join the paragraphs either side. Each paragraph changes something; one that restates the paragraph before is deleted.
- The last paragraph does not summarise. End on the last useful fact, ask or image.
- Bullets: no bold-label-colon on every item. Lists hold facts, not slogans.

## Headlines
- A claim or outcome in plain words, 6 to 12 words, no colon-subtitle pairs ("X: a journey to Y").
- Three shapes that work: the plain claim ("Three deployment modes, one API"); the question the reader already has ("Where does the index actually rest?"); number plus noun ("Four questions that qualify a retrieval deal").

## Calls to action
- One ask per piece, concrete and small: "Book a 30-minute scoping call", "Reply with the one document set you'd test first".
- Never "Learn more", "Reach out", "Let's connect" or "Thoughts?".

## LinkedIn posts
- Hook in line one, under 15 words, never "I'm excited". Paragraphs of 1 to 2 lines. 120 to 220 words per post.
- 0 to 3 hashtags. End with a question that has a real answer, or a concrete take. The owner's personal posts may keep em dashes; nothing else may.

## Emails
- Subject under 50 characters, no colon, no exclamation mark. First line says why this reader, now.
- 90 to 150 words, one idea, one ask, at most one link. Placeholders in square brackets: [First Name], [Account Name].
- Sign-off block left for the rep. First line of the file: a DRAFT status line until signed off.
